title: Silent 5xx Pattern Analysis — Hosted API (intermittent streaming + latency)
content:
SUMMARY:
On 2026-03-09 UTC we observed a ~40 minute window of intermittent 5xx errors and elevated tail latency across several Hosted API endpoints, with the most severe user impact on streaming responses. The incident manifested as a pattern of silent 5xx bursts (many 502/503/504) accompanied by connection resets during streaming handshake phases. Total error rate peaked at ~4.3% for tenant-facing traffic and caused degraded UX for customers using streaming SDKs and long-polling integrations.

PRIORITY / IMPACT:
- Severity: P0 (customer-facing outage with error & latency SLO breaches)
- Affected: Hosted API (us-west-2 primary region), spillover to eu-west-1 for some routes due to failovers
- Duration: ~2026-03-09 17:12 UTC — 17:52 UTC (root cause #1 mitigated by 17:30; full stabilization by 17:52)
- Customer visible: SDK stream reconnect storms, increased 5xx counts in dashboards, higher 99th percentile latency for token-generation routes

DETECTION:
- First signal: Anomalous increase in 502/503 rates alerted by per-route 5xx monitor at 17:14 UTC (pager triggered to on-call SRE)
- Secondary signals: Telemetry spikes in connection-reset metric and streaming handshake failures logged in edge-proxy traces
- Early notes: Alerts showed bursty pattern, not continuous; some requests succeeded while nearby requests failed (intermittent).

INITIAL TRIAGE (timeline highlights):
- 17:14 UTC: Pager received (Aisha). Slack incident channel created (#sre-incident-2026-03-09).
- 17:16 UTC: Confirmed error spike via dashboards; scope looked regional (us-west-2) but some routes in eu-west-1 saw latency due to reroutes.
- 17:18 UTC: Observed increased TCP RSTs and HTTP/1.1 connection resets in edge-proxy logs; streaming module showed many 'handshake timeout' traces.
- 17:22 UTC: Noted recent CDN/edge configuration rollout (infra PR#3421) completed at ~16:50 UTC and a canary to 20% was expanded to 100% at 16:58 UTC.
- 17:26 UTC: Rollback of last CDN header-rate-limit tuning initiated (infra) -> partial reduction in 502s seen by 17:30 UTC.
- 17:34 UTC: Enabled additional circuit-breaker throttle on streaming routes; retries were constrained and connection reset storms subsided.
- 17:48 UTC: Full traffic normalization; follow-up verification until 17:52 UTC.

ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS (hypothesis & evidence):
- Primary contributor: A recent CDN/edge configuration change (PR#3421) altered upstream keepalive and header-throttling behavior. Under bursty streaming client reconnect patterns this change caused upstream edge nodes to drop or reset connections more aggressively, producing 5xx responses upstream rather than graceful 429 or retryable failures. Evidence: timing of rollout (16:58) correlates with onset; edge logs show increased connection termination policies and 'rate-limited header' events.

- Secondary contributor: Service-side retry/backoff behavior for streaming handshakes lacked a global circuit breaker for cross-route retry storms. Many SDKs retried aggressively on perceived transient failures, creating a feedback loop that overloaded proto-handshake path and amplified error rates. Evidence: request traces show clustered retries from same client IPs within seconds.

- Tertiary contributor: Observability gap — streaming handshake failures were logged in raw edge traces but not surfaced as structured alerts or grouped errors in long-term logs, making early RCA slower. We lacked a compact metric for 'stream-handshake-failure-rate' and per-tenant breakdown during the incident.

WHY DID THE CDN CHANGE CAUSE 5XX INSTEAD OF 429?
- The CDN's new header/keepalive policy caused some connections to be torn down mid-handshake. Downstream app servers interpreted abrupt upstream TCP resets as 502/504 errors. The edge did not map the termination cause into a structured 429 or backoff signal our stack can act on. This resulted in opaque 5xx spikes without clear upstream root reasons in application logs.

MITIGATION & CONTAINMENT ACTIONS (what we did in incident):
- 17:26 UTC: Infra rolled back the CDN header-rate-limit tuning to prior stable config (PR rollback). Partial improvement observed by 17:30.
- 17:34 UTC: Application team deployed temporary circuit-breaker patch for streaming handshake path, capping retry fanout per client IP and per-tenant.
- 17:36 UTC: Traffic rebalanced away from a small subset of edge nodes showing high drop rates; ops bumped healthy-region capacity to reduce failover load.
- 17:40 UTC: Customer comms (CS) notified major customers on affected plans with status teaser and ETA for update.

RUNBOOK & PROCESS GAPS IDENTIFIED:
- Missing runbook entry: No explicit rollback CTA for CDN header/keepalive changes when streaming handshakes degrade. Existing runbooks focused on rate-limiter rollbacks but not header/keepalive semantics.
- Insufficient alerting: We lack a high-signal metric for streaming handshake failures; per-route 5xx alert exists but does not differentiate handshake-reset patterns vs. application errors.
- Ownership ambiguity: CDN config changes are in infra repo but operational ownership for streaming-sensitive parameters sits with serving runtime team; rollout approvals did not include SRE streaming owners.
- Client SDK behavior: SDKs retry aggressively without jitter/backoff that respects per-tenant circuit-breakers — this was a multiplier for the outage.

ACTIONS / NEXT STEPS (owners & ETA):
Short-term (days):
- Infra: Add a pre-rollout gating checklist requiring SRE streaming owner signoff for header/keepalive related PRs. Owner: Diego. ETA: 2026-03-12.
- SRE: Create and instrument a 'streaming-handshake-failure-rate' metric with per-region and per-tenant tags; add an alert threshold. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2026-03-11.
- Runtime: Ship permanent circuit-breaker and standardized retry-policy enforcement in streaming library (limit retries per IP/tenant, add jitter). Owner: Tomislav. ETA: 2026-03-19.
- SDKs: Update official SDKs to adopt exponential backoff with capped retries for streaming connect attempts. Owner: Maya (developer-experience). ETA: 2026-03-23.

Long-term (weeks -> quarters):
- Observability: Add structured edge -> app error mapping so edge termination reasons surface as typed events (e.g., HEADER_TRUNCATED, KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT) instead of opaque 5xx. Owner: Eng Observability. ETA: 2026-Q2.
- Runbooks: Expand CDNs/edge rollout runbook to include explicit rollback triggers for streaming-sensitive parameters and safe canary rollout sizes for streaming-heavy routes. Owner: eng-sre + infra. ETA: 2026-03-30.
- Chaos & Testing: Add synthetic streaming handshake load tests in CI to validate header/keepalive changes under retry/backoff storms. Owner: serving-runtime + release-eng. ETA: 2026-04-15.

COMMUNICATIONS & CUSTOMER FOLLOW-UP:
- CS already sent preliminary notice; follow-up with detailed RCA draft by 2026-03-12.
- For customers with repeat streaming usage, offer proactive guidance on SDK retry settings and recommended tokenization chunk sizes to reduce reconnects. Owner: customer-success. ETA: 2026-03-16.

LESSONS LEARNED (short form):
- CDN/edge changes can produce failure modes that our stack maps into opaque 5xx; we need explicit mappings and pre-rollout SRE reviews for streaming-sensitive parameters.
- Small config changes + aggressive client retries = feedback storms. Circuit breakers and conservative retry policies are first-class protections.
- Observability must include handshake-level metrics for long-lived connections (streams, websockets).

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs:
- Can the CDN/edge vendor provide richer termination reason codes we can ingest? (action: Diego to ask vendor; ETA: 2026-03-11)
- Do we want per-tenant emergency throttles that SRE can flip without infra deploys? (proposal: create a feature flag-backed throttle endpoint)
- How to include SDK authors in rollout approval loops without slowing release velocity? (proposal: automated impact analysis + quick SRE signoff)

NOTES TO SELF / CHATTY ITEMS (informal):
- We were lucky the rollback was quick; if rollout had been to a region with higher traffic the impact would have been worse. Need automated canary size enforcement.
- Some of the initial noise came from a monitoring dashboard not updating on timezone config — fix that separately (tiny ops pain).

APPENDICES / DATA SAMPLES:
- Sample edge trace snippet showing repeated handshake attempts and TCP reset deltas (available in linked artifacts / logs).
- Raw alert graph links: (attached to ticket JIRA-INC-1248).

OWNER(S) FOR RCA/POSTMORTEM: Aisha Rahman (eng-sre), Diego Martinez (infra), Priya Nair (observability), Tomislav Horvat (serving-runtime), Maya Lee (devx).

STATUS: Draft RCA; seeking review from infra, serving-runtime, and devx owners. Once agreed we'll publish a customer-facing summary and close follow-up tickets.
